newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hogs sell steady-$1.00 lower - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hogs sell steady-$1.00 lower - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct hogs early Monday sold steady to $1.00 per cwt lower, pressured by improved weather after last week's harsh conditions and increased hog marketings, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.

Snow and cold in the Midwest late last week stalled hog marketings and forced packers to vigorously compete for animals. Temperatures were moderating and snow was melting early Monday, sparking ideas producers will bring ample hogs to market to meet packers' needs.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower at $52.00-$53.00/country and $53.50/plants.

Illinois hogs sold $1.00 lower at $52.00 to $53.00 in the country and $53.50 to $54.00 at plants. Hog movement was said to be "decent" and expected to grow larger as the day progressed, one Illinois buyer said.
Indiana hogs sold $1.00 lower at $51.50 to $52.50 in the country and $53.50 to $54.00 at plants.
"It looks quiet early, but there should be just enough hogs," a central Indiana hog buyer said.
Ohio hogs sold $0.50 lower at $51.00 to $52.00 in the country and up to $54.00 at plants, dealers said.
